title: Algebraic reading: Hecke spectral-gap closure

Remark. Algebraic reading: Hecke spectral-gap closure

Rooted in the precise categorical origin of the crossing energy, executing the limit q \to 1 directly forces the Hecke spectral-gap closure. The two eigenvalues (q, -q^{-1}) driving the Hecke generator \sigma across V \otimes V collide mechanically at (1, -1). The structural buffer separating the symmetric and antisymmetric transport channels erases entirely.

  • The obstruction class \mathrm{NS}(A) tracks the failure of the q-deformed transport mechanism to sustain diagonalisation as q \to 1.
  • Blowup of globally smooth solutions corresponds directly to the Markov trace's failure to separate S^{2} V away from \Lambda^{2} V inside the classical limit. It operates as an algebraic collapse, parallel to but distinct from classical continuous-energy blowup models.
  • \mathrm{NS}(A) = 0 triggers only if the categorical volume constraint survives the q \to 1 limit rigidly intact. This happens exclusively when a codimension-\geq 2 locus governs the classical limit inside the eigenvalue moduli.

This supplies an algebraic failure criterion ruling smoothness. It abandons continuous energy estimates entirely, testing the obstruction merely by verifying if the Hecke spectral gap closes cleanly to first order or higher order in (q - 1).
